eas_text: A civil authority has issued AN IMMEDIATE EVACUATION NOTICE for the following counties or areas: Newaygo, MI; at 7:04 AM on AUG 15, 2023 Effective until 9:34 AM. Message from WSLF/CAP.
extra_text:
TEST MESSAGE ONLY! - A FLASH FLOOD WARNING for the Muskegon River below the Hardy Dam has been issued due to failure of the Hardy Dam. Water is moving at speeds outside survivable conditions. Anyone below the dam within 1 mile of the Muskegon River should IMMEDIATELY move to higher ground away from the river.  Emergency assistance will not be available to persons choosing not to adhere to this warning. Anyone within the area should immediately follow the emergency instructions below!  
 
TAKE ACTION NOW IF YOU ARE WITHIN 1 MILE OF THE MUSKEGON RIVER 

	Move to higher ground immediately - at least 1 mile away from the Muskegon River! Water is moving at speeds outside survivable conditions and significant erosion is expected.
	Call 9-1-1 to report a life-threatening emergency!  If you are trapped and need immediate assistance evacuating the area, call 9-1-1.
	Follow all instructions given by Public Safety Officials! Law Enforcement officers and firefighters are working to get individuals out of the area to safety.
	Do not use any bridge crossing over the Muskegon River! All bridge crossings are being closed and expected to be destroyed by flash flood waters.
	Report to evacuation shelters for emergency assistance! 
	
		Residents on the East of South sides of the Muskegon River should go to Grant Middle School at 96 E 120th Street, Grant, MI 49327
		Residents on the West and North sides of the Muskegon River should go to Harvest Church in Fremont at 5479 W 72nd Street, Fremont, MI 49412.
	
	
	Emergency Assistance will not be available to persons choosing not to adhere to this warning! 

 
This message will be updated with further information and instructions as soon as possible!
 
WHAT TO EXPECT


	Rapidly rising water levels within minutes! Water levels may rise as fast as 2 ft per minute in some areas.
	Historic, catastrophic flooding on the Muskegon River below Hardy Dam. Maximum rises in water levels are expected to be anywhere from 20 feet to 62 feet high. 
	Approximately 1,896 homes and businesses below the Hardy Dam near the Muskegon River are anticipated to be destroyed by flash flood waters. Significant loss of life and property is expected for anyone remaining in the area within 1 mile of the Muskegon River.
	All bridge crossings over the Muskegon River are closed. All bridge crossings are expected to be destroyed by flash flood waters.   
	
		Structure #7734 – Croton Drive over the Muskegon River (Section 18 Croton Twp)
		M37 Bridge over the Muskegon River (City of Newaygo)
		Bridge Street Bridge over the Muskegon River (City of Newaygo)
		Structure #7740 – Warner Ave over the Muskegon River (Section 13/14 Bridgeton)
		Maple Island Bridge over the Muskegon River (Bridgeton Township)
	
	
	Approximately 65 roadways to be closed around the Muskegon River. Multiple roadways are expected to be destroyed by flash flood waters.
	Loss of infrastructure systems including power, cell phones, cable, internet, and natural gas. Widespread outages are expected for power, cell phone, internet, cable, and natural gas due to the destruction of utilities. Loss of City of Newaygo municipal fresh water and wastewater Systems are also expected.
	Restricted access into the area! Areas below the Hardy Dam within 1 mile of the Muskegon River should expect to be restricted to the public in order to get emergency resources in the disaster areas quickly and minimize public exposure to dangerous conditions that will prevail.
	Temporary FAA flight restrictions for a five mile radius around the Muskegon River from Mecosta County to Lake Michigan. This airspace will be restricted for authorized disaster response air support resources only. NO use of drones is permitted in this area.       
	Emergency assistance will not be available to persons choosing not to adhere to this warning. 

 
COMMUNITY INFORMATION


	ONLY CALL 9-1-1 TO REPORT EMERGENCIES!   Emergency operators and phone lines are needed to support this incident, please continue to monitor Nixle for updates or call 2-1-1 (not 9-1-1) for general safety information.
	AVOID THE AREA WITHIN 1 MILE OF THE MUSKEGON RIVER! Water is moving at speeds outside of survivable river conditions. These conditions include extreme currents, high water, dangerous debris, and bank collapse. The public is being directed avoid the area until further notice. Emergency assistance will not be available to persons choosing not to adhere to this warning.
	REQUEST TO RELEASE PUBLIC SAFETY EMPLOYEES TO EMERGENCY DUTIES! To ensure maximum capability in emergency response, all government, public, and private entities within the County of Newaygo shall release employees for emergency duties.  This includes auxiliary firefighters, police officers, emergency medical personnel, emergency management, and volunteer support persons (i.e. Community Emergency Response Team and Medical Reserve Corps, American Red Cross, Salvation Army, etc.).
	ADDITIONAL INFORMATION WILL BE RELEASED!   Continue monitoring your radio, Nixle, and Newaygo County’s Website for additional information. Text NewaygoES to 888777 to sign up for Nixle or click here: https://local.nixle.com/register/. Due to expected outages, updated information will also be posted at local unaffected City and Township Halls within Newaygo County.  
	THANK YOU FOR YOUR COOPERATION! TEST MESSAGE ONLY! - EVACUATE NOW! A Flash Flood Warning has been issued for the Muskegon River for failure of the Hardy Dam. Water is moving at speeds outside survivable conditions. Anyone below the dam within 1 mile of the Muskegon River should IMMEDIATELY move to higher ground away from the river. Remain out of this area until further notice.
